title: Single-nucleus proteomics identifies regulators of protein transport
summary: A preprint first posted June18,2024 linked protein-abundance variation across3,412 macrophage-like-cell nuclei to LPS-induced nucleocytoplasmic transport, then tested16 candidate regulators by knockdown;13 conditions changed transport in the expected direction. DIA-NN v1.8.1 neural-network processing identified and quantified proteins from mass-spectrometry data, while weighted PCA and statistical associations drove downstream candidate nomination. The November22,2026 v2 retains this measurement role and13-of-16 result. AI supported proteomic measurement rather than directly predicting regulators; the findings concern a cell-model study, not a demonstrated clinical intervention.
ai_technology: DIA-NN v1.8.1 neural-network-based data-independent acquisition proteomics processing
organization: Northeastern University; Parallel Squared Technology Institute

evidence.tested: DIA-NN processed mass-spectrometry measurements; 13/16 targeted knockdown conditions changed transport in the predicted direction.
evidence.unknown: The incremental contribution of DIA-NN versus another processing pipeline was not assessed here. Only13 of16 perturbation conditions changed transport in the expected direction; this is not confirmation of every candidate or evidence of clinical benefit.
evidence.ai_role: Neural-network-based DIA-NN searches used in-silico-predicted spectral libraries to identify and quantify proteins, enabling high-depth proteomic measurement used for regulator prioritization.

source_review.scope: Primary latest bioRxiv v2 PDF: DIA-NN raw-search Methods and knockdown Results; v1 PMC primary XML abstract/computational Methods/Results; primary DIA-NN method-paper XML for neural signal/noise processing; primary API version history. Versions retain3,412 nuclei and13/16 directional effects.
